decision.rationale: Lire le code AVX-512 à accumulateurs multiples de de7 pour examiner cette alternative au meilleur candidat Gm1 avant de choisir une intégration; sa moyenne globale est légèrement moins bonne, sans données par taille.

Intégrer à Gm1 le chemin AVX-512 à quatre accumulateurs de de7, tout en conservant le chemin AVX2 en un passage et les replis de Gm1. Gm1 est le meilleur candidat mesuré (1,042 µs); de7 est légèrement plus lent seul (1,058 µs), mais ses accumulateurs indépendants pourraient aider sur les grands tableaux. Les moyennes agrégées ne tranchent pas par taille; le contrôleur devra mesurer cette combinaison correcte avant de conclure.

Les deux premières intégrations sont correctes mais plus lentes que Gm1. Parcourir des résultats divers pour repérer une idée distincte qui pourrait améliorer Gm1 sans reprendre ces variantes perdantes.

model_interpretation.claim: Pour n≥64, quatre accumulateurs de minimum AVX-512 indépendants pourraient réduire la dépendance sérielle du chemin AVX-512 de Gm1, tout en conservant sa recherche ordonnée du premier indice. L’adaptation peut toutefois coûter davantage qu’elle ne gagne; les temps agrégés de Gm1 (1,042 µs) et de de7 (1,058 µs) ne permettent pas de conclure par taille.

model_interpretation.claim: The seven measured catalog programs are distinct; 07d45883e07a46ed remains fastest at 1.0536 μs, while de7d5ff03cf741e9 measured 1.0582 μs and the AVX2 block-local reduction 423673b4cff24d44 measured 7.4087 μs. This experiment tests a different one-pass mechanism: pack signed-value rank and index into an ordered 64-bit key, then use four AVX-512 qword-minimum accumulators. Avoiding the winner's second scan may offset key packing and the halved lane count, but the earlier results make a slowdown plausible; the official protocol must decide.
model_interpretation.transformations: {"files":["src/candidate.cpp"],"retained":["On AVX-512F builds and n >= 32, process groups of 32 integers as four eight-lane vectors, encoding each signed value's order and its index into a signed-comparable 64-bit key.","Maintain four independent SIMD minimum accumulators, combine them for one horizontal minimum, decode the index, and compare encoded scalar-tail keys so equal values select the earliest index without rereading the input.","Retain the strict-less-than scalar argmin for small inputs or builds without AVX-512F; do not mutate the input or use additional threads."]}

model_interpretation.claim: The catalog reports 12 distinct programs in 12 trials, with no repeats. The four-way scalar unroll and four-element block reduction have nearly equal aggregate means (3.6437 and 3.6483 μs); the three-lane result is 3.7843 μs, while the scalar-register scan measured about 8.91 μs. These aggregate means do not establish per-size results, and recent candidates are close in performance. This contrasting eight-element balanced block reduction tests whether fewer global-best merges offset the extra local reduction work; it may instead lose to the four-element block. Correctness and official timings at both timed sizes should decide.

children.objective: Explore an explicitly vectorized argmin scan using x86 SIMD intrinsics where supported by the build target. Reduce values and recover the smallest matching index correctly; handle tails and all valid n. Compare viable vector widths or reduction strategies using the official correctness and timing protocol. Do not rely on test-value assumptions or exceed the one-thread budget.
children.subject: Explicit SIMD argmin reduction

children.objective: First test a scalar rewrite that keeps the best value in a register alongside its index, rather than comparing through the baseline's changing a[j] expression; preserve strict-less-than updates so ties select the earliest index. Then explore loop forms and modest independent partial accumulators/unrolling, merging partial results by value and then smallest index. Use no explicit x86 intrinsics or parallel execution. Validate all valid sizes and input patterns, and compare official timings at both timed sizes; compiler transformation of the baseline is unknown, so judge by measured results.
